story: Robert A Lindquist is a middle author on two cell-biology papers in the Atlas. The 2007 paper identified PRAS40 as an insulin-controlled brake inside mTORC1: without insulin PRAS40 holds the complex shut, and insulin makes Akt phosphorylate PRAS40 so the brake lets go. The 2008 paper found that the Rag GTPases bind raptor and let mTORC1 sense amino acids, by controlling whether mTOR sits near its activator Rheb.

PubMed does not list an affiliation for him in these two records. The link to the Whitehead Institute comes from a related paper from the same group (a Drosophila RNAi screen of TORC1 signaling), where PubMed lists him there and where several co-authors of the Atlas papers also appear.

highlights.SAN2007: Middle author of the paper on PRAS40 as an insulin-regulated inhibitor of mTORC1.

studies.title: The Rag GTPases bind raptor and mediate amino acid signaling to mTORC1

studies.title: PRAS40 is an insulin-regulated inhibitor of the mTORC1 protein kinase
studies.finding: Identified PRAS40 as the missing insulin-controlled brake INSIDE mTORC1. When insulin is absent PRAS40 clamps the complex shut; insulin makes Akt phosphorylate PRAS40, releasing the brake so Rheb can fully switch mTORC1 on. Explained how hormone signals set the exact strength of mTORC1 activity.

story: Xin Gu is first author of a 2017 cell study that found SAMTOR, a protein that senses S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the cell's methyl donor. When methionine runs low, SAM falls, SAMTOR binds GATOR1 and mTORC1 signalling is reduced. This extends nutrient sensing from amino acids to a metabolite.

PubMed also lists Gu, at the same Whitehead Institute and MIT address, as a middle author of three further papers: the 2017 KICSTOR study (a complex that holds GATOR1 on the lysosome), the 2019 cryo-EM structure of Raptor docked on Rag-Ragulator, and the 2022 cryo-EM structure of GATOR2.

studies.title: SAMTOR is an S-adenosylmethionine sensor for the mTORC1 pathway

studies.title: Structural basis for the docking of mTORC1 on the lysosomal surface
studies.finding:
3.2-angstrom cryo-EM structure of Raptor bound to Rag-Ragulator, showing how Raptor reads out the nutrient-dependent nucleotide state of the Rag GTPases: one part of Raptor senses RagA's nucleotide state, a separate 'claw' senses RagC's, and both have to be in the correct nutrient-signalling combination before Raptor is allowed to dock. Mutating the contact points blocks mTORC1 from reaching the lysosome and inhibits its signalling, which is the functional evidence behind the structural claim. Combined with a separate structure of mTORC1 bound to its activator Rheb, the paper builds a model of the complete, active mTORC1 sitting on the lysosome.

studies.title: Structure of the nutrient-sensing hub GATOR2
studies.finding: Cryo-EM structure of human GATOR2: a 1.1 MDa, two-fold symmetric cage built on an octagonal scaffold decorated with eight pairs of WD40 beta-propellers, and a map of where Sestrin2 and CASTOR1 dock. It substantially advances the GATOR2 side of the sensor module, though how GATOR2 inhibits GATOR1 is still not fully settled.

studies.title: Lysosomal metabolomics reveals V-ATPase- and mTOR-dependent regulation of amino acid efflux from lysosomes
studies.finding: Turns the lysosome from a place where mTORC1 is switched on into something mTORC1 also controls: inhibiting mTOR strongly reduces the efflux of most essential amino acids out of the lysosome, so the organelle becomes a store rather than a source. Measured directly by rapidly isolating lysosomes and profiling their contents, which is why the claim is about concentrations inside the organelle and not inferred from signalling readouts. Boundary: one human cell line, acute pharmacological inhibition.

story: Eric Spooner is a co-author on two papers in the Atlas, both listed at the Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He is a middle author on both.

The 2013 paper showed that folliculin acts as a GAP for RagC/D, helping amino acids switch on mTORC1 at the lysosome. The 2014 paper showed that Sestrins bind GATOR2 to dampen the amino-acid signal. Both are cell studies. A third Atlas paper from 2007 lists the same name, but its PubMed record gives no affiliation for him, so it is not covered here.

story: Zhi-Yang Tsun was first author of the Atlas study TSU2013 in Molecular Cell. Working in cells, the paper showed that the folliculin tumour suppressor, together with FNIP, acts as a GAP (an activating helper) for the RagC and RagD GTPases. Rag proteins carrying GDP are needed to bind mTORC1 and bring it to the lysosome, where amino acids switch it on.

Tsun is also a middle author of WAN2015 in Science, which reported that the lysosomal transporter SLC38A9 signals arginine sufficiency to mTORC1. PubMed lists both papers at the Whitehead Institute and the MIT Department of Biology.

story: BAR2013 (2013) is a cell study that found GATOR1, a protein complex that switches off the Rag proteins and so turns mTORC1 down when amino acids run low. GATOR1 genes are mutated in some cancers, which made those cancer cells keep mTORC1 on and more sensitive to rapamycin. Kathleen Ottina is a middle author in the author list. HSU2011 (2011) is a cell study that mapped which phosphate tags on proteins depend on mTOR and found that Grb10 is an mTORC1 target that helps turn down growth-factor signalling. Kathleen Ottina is a middle author in the author list.
PubMed lists Kathleen A Ottina in both records but gives no affiliation for her there. Two related papers from the same laboratory list her at the Whitehead Institute and MIT.

highlights.HSU2011: Middle author of this paper on the mTOR phosphoproteome.

studies.title: A Tumor suppressor complex with GAP activity for the Rag GTPases that signal amino acid sufficiency to mTORC1
studies.finding: Found the OFF switch for amino acid signaling: the GATOR1 complex is a GAP that shuts the Rag GTPases (and thus mTORC1) down when amino acids run low, while GATOR2 opposes it. GATOR1 genes are mutated in cancers, making those tumors 'blind' to starvation and hypersensitive to rapamycin.

story: In fruit flies, mutations in the Rheb gene stopped cell growth, while extra Rheb made cells grow more. The genetic and biochemical tests put Rheb downstream of Tsc1-Tsc2 in the TOR pathway, with S6K as a main effector.

Hugo Stocker is first author. PubMed lists him at the Zoological Institute of the University of Zurich. Two other Atlas records under this name lack a full given name or an affiliation, so only this paper is included.

story: This 2025 review looks at human evidence for low-dose rapamycin and related drugs in healthy adults, and re-models one cohort with the PhenoAge biological-age clock. Its conclusion is cautious: animal lifespan data are strong, but human data have not yet shown that rapamycin delays aging in healthy people.
Bradley Rosen is the last author. PubMed lists his affiliation only as mTOR Medicine Practitioner, Los Angeles.

pubmed_affiliation: mTOR Medicine Practitioner, Los Angeles, CA 90212, USA.

studies.title: What is the clinical evidence to support off-label rapamycin therapy in healthy adults?
studies.finding: A deliberately cautious review of low-dose rapamycin in healthy adults, and re-models one cohort using the PhenoAge biological-aging clock. Verdict: despite strong animal lifespan data, human evidence does NOT yet prove rapamycin delays aging in healthy people. A valuable counterweight to longevity-community hype - it holds the human evidence to a strict standard rather than over-reading promising signals.

current.role: Senior (last) author of the 2021 phase 2b and phase 3 trials of the mTOR inhibitor RTB101 in older adults.
story: Sarb Shergill was last author of a 2021 Lancet Healthy Longevity paper in the Atlas (MAN2021), with seven co-authors listed at resTORbio. It reports two trials of RTB101, a drug that blocks mTOR, given daily for 16 weeks to adults over 65. In the phase 2b trial, fewer people on 10 mg had a lab-confirmed respiratory infection, but the result came from a pooled analysis and the corrected analysis was not significant. The phase 3 trial showed no drop in respiratory illness.

highlights.MAN2021: Last author; PubMed lists the author at resTORbio in Boston.

studies.title: Targeting the biology of ageing with mTOR inhibitors to improve immune function in older adults: phase 2b and phase 3 randomised trials
studies.finding: This paper reports two trials of RTB101, a drug that blocks mTOR, taken once a day for 16 weeks by adults over 65. In the phase 2b trial (652 people), fewer people on 10 mg had a lab-confirmed respiratory infection than on placebo (19% against 28%), but that result comes from a pooled analysis the authors did not correct for multiple testing, and the corrected analysis did not reach significance. The phase 3 trial (1,024 people) used a different main endpoint, set with the FDA: symptoms with or without a lab test.
